children: Euronext wheat fell on Tuesday as a sharp drop in Chicago prices outweighed earlier support from talk of fresh export demand for EU wheat, traders said.
settled 0.8% down at €241.50 ($271.28) a metric ton after the main session.
In choppy trading, the benchmark contract rose to €247.50, approaching a one-month peak struck last week, before turning lower and hitting its lowest since October 9.
dropped by around 1.7% to a fresh two-month low, after steadying earlier in the day.
Grain markets tracked a reversal in crude oil, which added to background pressure from advancing US corn and soybean harvests.
Headlines about ongoing diplomatic discussions to end Russia's war with Ukraine also curbed prices, dealers said.
Market worries about war disruption to Black Sea exports have also been tempered by rising Russian shipments through the Baltic Sea.
Latvia, a member of the European Union and NATO, has emerged as one of the top five importers of Russian grain this season as Moscow redirects exports to Baltic ports, consultancy ProZerno said.
Euronext nonetheless remained underpinned by importers switching to EU origins for some of the volumes usually sourced from Russia and Ukraine.
Talk in particular that buyers in Egypt, the world's biggest wheat-importing country, were inquiring about EU wheat supported earlier gains on Euronext, traders said.
Weekly EU data showed the bloc's soft wheat exports so far in 2026/27 were stable year on year at 8.47 million tons, though export figures remained incomplete for several countries.
The data also showed EU maize imports so far this season were up 40%, illustrating the bloc's needs in the face of a weather-hit harvest marked by the smallest French crop in 50 years.
